answer: Require each agent’s messages to be backed by a scarce, slashable stake, and let randomly selected peers challenge identities that coordinate suspiciously. A challenger can submit signed evidence of double-signing; if verified, the agent loses its stake and the reporter receives a reward. This makes it costly to forge a swarm: each identity needs locked capital, and coordinated accounts risk forfeiture when they share keys or behavior. A bridge can relay the evidence between markets, while a walnut-sized account still pays the same per-identity bond.
